speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) which entity owns the copyright to the video recordings of parliamentary proceedings; and (b) if these video records are protected by copyright, whether the Ministry will consider removing such copyright and making all video footage of parliamentary proceedings freely available for use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: This practice is consistent with well-accepted online etiquette, and the arrangement has worked well so far.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Mediacorp's recordings have been regularly used by social media sites as well as political parties, including the Workers' Party.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is common in other developed countries and legislatures like Australia, Taiwan, Japan, UK, US and France, for example, many of whom have their YouTube channel or some other ways of archiving video recordings of sittings.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second one is: why does a corporate entity own the copyright to record a Parliamentary proceedings − an activity where other costs associated with creating the proceedings, such as the cost of the Parliament team, for example, are paid for by the taxpayers?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Why should a corporate entity be given so much power to choose what to put up, when to put it up, when to take it down, how to edit it before presentation?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And I do know from direct experience that, at times, these clips are edited and they are not archived and made available verbatim.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly, if the consideration behind this is cost, is it possible to rethink the allocation of cost by collecting fees on a pay-per-use basis from a variety of media outlets?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked about these issues and I have explained at that time to Mr Pritam Singh and others that the reason why we do not have a live feed is because this is not in great demand.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Just to recap what we discussed at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Perera has also mentioned that the copyright belongs to Mediacorp.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Perera also mentioned that the footages have been – I think he used the word "edited" – and he mentioned that not everything is shown.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They are edited to show, to arrange and to sort them out based on the speakers and the reply given.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If Mr Perera feels that there are certain examples that have been left out, maybe the Member can give me some specific examples and we will certainly look into those.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: There was a specific example where a clip was put up in relation to the Presidential Election Act debates.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: If my memory serves me well, it was in January or February and the clip that was put up of certain exchanges, there were certain bits removed.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: It was actually communicated with Mediacorp and, through the correspondence, they actually made the rectification and put up a different clip.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, I think that was resolved quite amicably.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: My point is that, in general, is it the case that all the clips that are put up are completely free of editing?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I think the Senior Minister of State himself conceded that there is a certain degree of editing.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, those decisions are decisions which involve a high level of discretion.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Should they be decisions handled by a private entity or should they be handled by a Government body subject to scrutiny, subject to questioning?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: When I said "editing", what I meant was Channel NewsAsia would take the footages and they would sort them out based on the person who asked the question, the person who answered, so as to make it more convenient for viewers to search and to access these footages.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is shown as per what was said in Parliament and what is reflected in Hansard, on the microsite and on the video footages of Facebook page and so on and so forth.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is important, Mr Speaker, that when we discuss such issues, we have to recognise, is there a problem that we need to solve?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And if no problem exists, I think one should not go around looking for imaginary problems to tackle.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is like having a hammer and then wanting to knock everything around you as though they are nails.
